exports.description: Sets page-level attributes before first paint, so nothing changes once the page has painted. Render it in `<head>` (`<head><ThemeScript nonce={nonce} /></head>` in a root layout), and put `suppressHydrationWarning` on `<html>`, whose attributes the script changes. Today it sets `data-nz-platform` (`apple` or `other`; the detection rule is on `themeScript`).

exports.description:
The script `ThemeScript` renders, for frameworks that inline it themselves (Astro: `<script is:inline set:html={themeScript} />`) or that allow it by hash under a strict CSP.

It sets `data-nz-platform` on `<html>`: `"apple"` when the platform string matches `/mac|iphone|ipad|ipod/i`, else `"other"`. The platform string is `navigator.userAgentData.platform` where the browser has it (Chromium: `"macOS"`, `"Windows"`, …), else `navigator.platform` (`"MacIntel"`, `"iPhone"`, `"iPad"`; iPadOS reports `"MacIntel"`, which is still Apple). It never reads the user-agent string. An attribute already on `<html>` (set by the server, or by a test) is kept. Kbd reads the attribute to show `⌘K` or `Ctrl+K`.

Persisting the user's theme choice (§7.4) is not in this script yet.

Under a strict CSP, allow it by hash: `script-src 'sha256-HZHIu/4RWssbJrteyX51NbvdyR6ZSlZlY4BPl3yXw+I='`. The hash changes only when the script does, and a change is called out in the changelog.
exports.name: themeScript
